claims.text: Nearly simultaneous reduction of all metal precursors is the key determinant of homogeneous noble metal–based high-entropy alloy nanoparticle formation.
Nearly simultaneous precursor reduction promotes synchronous nucleation.
Synchronous nucleation kinetically traps an atomically mixed high-entropy state before segregation occurs.
The proposed initial material is a uniformly and atomically mixed precursor containing noble and associated metals in ionic form.
Adjusting heating uniformity or reagent delivery can enforce near-synchronous reduction without changing the overall chemical makeup.
Rapid, uniform heating with minimized local temperature and concentration gradients causes the constituent metals to reduce closer together in time.
Upon simultaneous reduction, an atomically mixed precursor transforms into a homogeneous amorphous or very fine-grained metallic phase.
The homogeneous amorphous or very fine-grained metallic phase can evolve into the desired alloy nanoparticles.
Concurrently reduced metal ions form nuclei that coalesce before thermodynamic driving forces can cause elemental segregation.
Sequential nucleation promotes phase separation or elemental segregation.
Relative to an asynchronous baseline, the modified process should produce nanoparticles with more uniform elemental distributions.
Relative to an asynchronous baseline, the modified process should produce a narrower particle-size distribution.
Relative to an asynchronous baseline, the modified process should preserve greater surface-atom exposure.
Conventional reaction inhomogeneities permit differences in reduction timing that result in phase separation, segregation, or uneven nanoparticle morphology.
The proposed mechanism should apply when precursor mixing is homogeneous and the variance among constituent reduction potentials is moderate.
The proposed mechanism may not apply when constituent redox characters are extremely disparate or other kinetic destabilizing factors dominate.
The relationship between reduction synchrony and final alloy homogeneity may vary with metal combination, synthesis scale, and reaction environment.
